title: Paid and Free Server Scheduling
statement:
A team must run `n` long-running tasks on two servers: a **paid** server and a **free** server. Task `i` costs `cost[i]` to run on the paid server and takes `time[i]` units of time there. Running a task on the free server costs nothing, and the free server finishes **any** task in exactly `1` unit of time, regardless of `time[i]`.

The rules are:

- Each task is run on exactly one of the two servers.
- The paid server runs one task at a time. While it is busy, you pay for the tasks it runs.
- The free server may only be used **while the paid server is busy** (some task is running on it). It also runs one task at a time.
- Tasks may be started in any order.

So if the paid server runs a set of tasks for a total of `T` units of time, the free server can run at most `T` tasks during that time, and every task that is not on the paid server must fit within these `T` units. At least one task must therefore run on the paid server.

Find the minimum total cost to run all `n` tasks.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `cost[0..n-1]`.
The third line contains `n` integers `time[0..n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum total cost.

examples.explanation: Run task 0 on the paid server for cost 1. It takes 3 units, during which the free server runs the other three tasks (1 unit each). Total cost 1.
Every paid task keeps the server busy for only 1 unit, so it can cover just one free task. Two paid tasks (the two with cost 2) are needed to cover the other two tasks. Total cost 4.
Paying for tasks 1 and 2 keeps the paid server busy for 2 units, so the free server can run task 0, whose paid cost would be 100. Total cost 2.

hints: If you choose a set S of tasks for the paid server, the other n - |S| tasks go to the free server. What condition on S makes this feasible?
Task i, when paid, handles itself plus time[i] free tasks, so it covers time[i] + 1 tasks. You need the covered total to reach at least n at minimum cost. This is a 0/1 knapsack in disguise.
Let dp[j] be the minimum cost to cover j tasks, capping j at n. Process each task once, iterating j downwards so a task is not used twice.
